title: Published multicolor CPV depths reject area-only changes under reported independent errors
abstract: We test a fixed dip spectrum with a free area scale in 51 published band depths of five complex periodic variable stars. Four stars have repeated filters. Under independent Gaussian errors at the reported scale, three reject this null at a four-test threshold of 0.05/4. The same-camera comparison of TIC 262400835 on two nights gives chi-square 14.07 for 3 degrees of freedom, p=0.00281. The test uses no effective wavelength and is invariant to any fixed band color correction or fixed companion dilution. For this star the result depends on z band; an added error floor of 0.085 percentage points makes the two-night result nonsignificant. This is conditional evidence for a change in occultation color, not a change in grain composition or material supply. Different clouds, changing stellar surface color, depth covariance and calibration remain possible causes. The source already reports variable color slopes. Our added result is a wavelength-free area test with fixed-color invariance and explicit error sensitivity. We provide code, aggregate results, an original figure, source hashes and separate-scratch repeat instructions.

display.caption: Published band depths tested against a fixed spectrum with a free area scale. Error assumptions limit the result.
